newsitem.title: USA: AmEx cuts 3,300 jobs in travel unit. [CORRECTED 22:46 GMT]
newsitem.headline: AmEx cuts 3,300 jobs in travel unit. [CORRECTED 22:46 GMT]

text.p: American Express Co on Monday said a restructuring in its Travel Related Service (TRS) unit will result in a reduction of 3,300 jobs from a worldwide work force of about 60,000.
The bulk of the job eliminations will occur overseas, with about 2,000 of the 3,300 TRS jobs being cut from the overseas workforce of 26,000.
The company announced in its fourth quarter earnings release that 3,300 positions will be cut and certain facilities will be consolidated.

Spokeswoman Susan Miller said in response to a question that some of the employees who will be affected by the restructuring have been alerted but for others details were still being worked out. She said the 3,300 figure represented both job eliminations and the number of people being let go.
Regarding the facilities to be consolidated, she said "they are not the major locations."

American Express said it was taking a $138 million after-tax restructuring charge in the fourth quarter, primarily related to TRS. Within TRS, the charge was $125 million after-tax and and $196 million pre-tax.

Asked about the amount of cost savings expected in the future, Miller said the restructuring steps were "part of our ongoing re-engineering initiatives which are designed to reduce our cost base so that we reinvest those savings into growth areas of the business."
The company has previously defined growth areas as international, financial services and its card network.

American Express also said its fourth quarter included a $300 million after-tax gain on the exchange of its debt exchangeable for common stock (DECS) for shares or common stock of First Data Corp. The exchange and the after-tax gain were originally announced in October. Miller said an increase in the share price of First Data led to the gain (corrects from transaction). American Express's stake in First Data has now been cut to about three million shares. In the exchange, DECS holders received First Data shares.
On an operating basis in the fourth quarter, American Express earned $433 million versus $384 million a year ago.

American Express shares were down 1-3/4 to 59-3/8 in late trading. Moshe Orenbuch, analyst at Sanford C. Bernstein Co, said the dip in the stock price may have reflected disappointment on the part of some investors that the cost savings in the restructuring would not flow to the bottom line, but instead would be reinvested in the business. He said that, while growth has improved for American Express in the last two quarters, the company is still wrestling with expenses. Asked if reinvesting the money was a good move for American Epxress, he said, "it's certainly the right thing to do and it's consistent with their attitude in the past."
Orenbuch, who has a neutral rating on the stock, said the company's cost structure is still significantly higher than bank card issuers.
Excluding the restructuring, TRS had operating income of $299 million in the fourth quarter versus $266 million a year ago.

American Express Financial Advisors had fourth quarter net income of $155 million versus $133 million. American Express Bank had net income of $17 million in the fourth quarter versus $21 million a year ago. Employment companywide at the end of the year was about 72,000 including the 60,000 in TRS.
